certificationCard.description: Certified Application Architects have a deep understanding of native Salesforce features and functionality. They're also experts at modeling a role hierarchy, data, and appropriate sharing mechanisms.

keyConcepts.h2: Application Architect: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Data Architecture: Object Design and Large Data Volumes
blocks.body: Application Architects design the data model to support business processes, sharing requirements, and performance. **Master-Detail** vs Lookup choice impacts cascade delete, sharing inheritance, roll-up summaries, and required relationship. **Junction objects** for many-to-many. External Objects for data federation. Large Data Volume (LDV) considerations — indexed fields, selective queries, skinny tables — must be built into the design, not retrofitted. The architect evaluates trade-offs between normalised and denormalised structures based on query patterns.

blocks.heading: Business Logic: Flow vs Apex Decision Matrix
blocks.body: Prefer declarative (Flow) over programmatic (**Apex**) when flows can handle the logic without governor limit concerns. Use Apex when: the logic is too complex for Flow, requires complex data manipulation, needs callouts, or has performance requirements that Flow cannot meet. **Platform Events** decouple systems — use for fire-and-forget async messaging. **Change Data Capture** streams record changes to external systems. The exam tests the trade-off decision at the architect level — maintainability, scalability, and test coverage requirements factor into the choice.

blocks.heading: Integration Architecture: Patterns and Tools
blocks.body: REST callouts for synchronous data retrieval. **Platform Events** for async, decoupled messaging. **Bulk API** 2.0 for high-volume data exchange. MuleSoft for complex orchestration, protocol translation, or multi-system fan-out. **Named Credentials** secure endpoint and auth configuration. The integration pattern selection depends on: synchronous vs asynchronous requirements, volume (Bulk API threshold is typically 200+ records), direction (inbound vs outbound), and latency requirements. The exam tests pattern selection based on these criteria.

blocks.heading: Security Architecture: Layered Access Design
blocks.body: Security design starts at the data model — **OWD** determines the record access baseline. **Role Hierarchy** grants manager visibility. **Sharing Rules** extend access. **Permission Sets** and **Permission Set Groups** manage object/field permissions. The architect must also consider Connected App policies, **OAuth** scopes, **Named Credentials**, Shield Platform Encryption for sensitive data, and Event Monitoring for audit. The exam tests holistic security design — identifying which layer to configure for a given access requirement.

blocks.heading: Declarative vs Programmatic Trade-offs
blocks.body: Architects make build-vs-configure decisions. Declarative tools (Flow, **Validation Rules**, Formula Fields, Approval Processes) are preferred for maintainability — no deployment complexity, admins can modify without code deployment. Programmatic code (**Apex**, **LWC**) is required for: complex conditional logic exceeding Flow capabilities, external system callouts requiring transformation, and UI patterns not achievable declaratively. The exam presents a business requirement and asks which combination of declarative and programmatic tools provides the best architecture, weighing complexity, maintainability, and scalability.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Application Architect Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Application Architect credential validates expertise in designing robust Salesforce applications. Questions test your ability to apply the right pattern — declarative vs. programmatic, which relationship type, which security model — for complex multi-requirement scenarios.

blocks.heading: Data Modeling for Scale
blocks.body: Know when to use lookup vs. **master-detail**, external objects (Salesforce Connect), big objects, and custom metadata types. Understand the impact of each relationship type on reporting, rollups, and data access.

blocks.heading: Security Architecture Layers
blocks.body: Understand how object-level, field-level, and **record-level security** interact. Know the order of evaluation and how to use the Access Checker to diagnose access issues in complex orgs.

blocks.heading: Apex Design Patterns
blocks.body: Know common design patterns: Singleton, Strategy, and Decorator for **Apex**. Understand trigger frameworks (one trigger per object pattern), virtual/abstract classes, and interface-based design for testability.

blocks.heading: Integration Patterns
blocks.body: Know the canonical integration patterns: Remote Process Invocation (request/reply and fire-and-forget), Data Virtualization, Batch Data Sync, and UI Update via Remote Process. Match each to REST/SOAP/**Platform Events**.

blocks.heading: Declarative vs. Programmatic Decision
blocks.body: Always justify when code is needed vs. when declarative tools suffice. Exam questions reward candidates who choose the simplest, most maintainable solution and understand the trade-offs.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the focus of an Application Architect?
options: Deep understanding of native Salesforce features and modeling role hierarchy, data, and sharing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Application Architects have deep understanding of native Salesforce features and model role hierarchy, data, and sharing.

sampleQuestions.question: Which sharing mechanism is used to open access based on record ownership?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing rules extend access based on ownership or criteria.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the role hierarchy used for?
options: Inheriting record access and roll-up for forecasts and reports
sampleQuestions.explanation: Role hierarchy controls record access inheritance and roll-up for reporting and forecasts.

sampleQuestions.question: Which certification is typically a prerequisite for Application Architect?
options: Platform Developer I and Sharing and Visibility Architect (or equivalent knowledge)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Application Architect builds on platform and sharing/visibility knowledge.

sampleQuestions.question: What does 'modeling data' mean for an Application Architect?
options: Designing object model, relationships, and data volume strategy
sampleQuestions.explanation: Modeling data includes object design, relationships, and data volume strategy.

sampleQuestions.question: What does Organization-Wide Defaults (OWD) control?
options: The baseline record access for each object (Private, Public Read Only, etc.)
sampleQuestions.explanation: OWD defines the default sharing model for each object.

sampleQuestions.question: Which mechanism extends access when OWD is Private?
options: Sharing rules, role hierarchy, and manual sharing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing rules, role hierarchy, and manual sharing extend access beyond OWD.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a criteria-based sharing rule?
options: To grant access to records that match specified criteria
sampleQuestions.explanation: Criteria-based sharing rules grant access based on field values.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Salesforce feature supports multi-tenant data isolation?
options: Sharing model, org ID, and platform architecture
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing model and org-level isolation provide multi-tenant security.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the development lifecycle for an Application Architect include?
options: Design, development, testing, deployment, and governance
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lifecycle spans design through deployment with governance.

sampleQuestions.question: Which relationship affects record-level security and roll-up?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Master-Detail affects sharing; child inherits parent's access.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a delegated admin group?
options: To grant limited admin capabilities to specific users
sampleQuestions.explanation: Delegated admin groups provide scoped admin access.

sampleQuestions.question: Which integration consideration applies to Application Architects?
options: Authentication, data ownership, and sharing for integrated data
sampleQuestions.explanation: Integration must consider auth, ownership, and sharing.

sampleQuestions.question: What does visibility mean in the sharing context?
options: Which records a user can see based on sharing rules and permissions
sampleQuestions.explanation: Visibility determines which records are visible to users.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best practice supports scalable role hierarchy design?
options: Keep hierarchy flat where possible; avoid deep nesting
sampleQuestions.explanation: Flatter hierarchies simplify sharing and maintenance.
